content: In this work, we look at the feasibility of training and tuning seq2seq-attention models towards a solution that generalizes in this linguistic sense. In particular, we train models on a symbol replacement task with a well defined generalizable structure. The task is simple enough that all models achieve near perfect accuracy on the standard test set, i.e., where the inputs are drawn from the same distribution as that of the training set. We then test these models for linguistic generalization by creating test sets of uncharacteristic inputs, i.e., inputs that are not typical in the training distribution but still solvable given that the generalizable structure was learned. Our results indicate that generalization is highly sensitive; such that even changes in the random seed can drastically affect the ability to generalize. This dependence on an element that is not (or ideally should not be) a hyperparameter suggests that the line between generalization and failure is quite fine, and may not be feasible to reach simply by hyperparameter tuning alone.
